The statement conveys a modestly dovish tilt: a 25 bp cut alongside “balanced risks” and continued balance-sheet runoff. Framing this through the literature, the Committee’s data dependence and symmetry around dual-mandate objectives align with flexible inflation targeting and loss-function-based policy (Svensson; Walsh). The gradual 25 bp move under uncertainty is consistent with “policy attenuation” or cautious gradualism (Brainard) and a rule-like, forward-looking reaction function (Clarida–Galí–Gertler; Rudebusch on funds-rate targeting). Implementation choices—setting ON RRP at the floor of the 4.25–4.50% range and IORB at 4.4%—fit corridor/floor-system guidance (Goodfriend) and support effective transmission to short-term funding markets. However, with inflation still above target and a dissent to hold, the New Keynesian Phillips-curve view (Calvo/Woodford) implies remaining inflation persistence, tempering the dovishness. Net tone: slightly positive relative to neutral.
